dedupe_keys.name: who global health expenditure database ghed

description: The Global Health Expenditure Database holds internationally comparable figures on how much each country spends on health and who pays for it. The World Health Organization produces it every year from national health accounts, government expenditure records and official statistics, filling gaps with estimates so that series are consistent across countries and years. Coverage is 194 to 195 countries and territories from 2000, with the latest update adding spending for 2023; indicators include current health expenditure per capita and as a share of GDP, government, household out-of-pocket and external donor shares, and for a growing number of countries breakdowns by health care function, primary health care, disease, provider type, children under five and capital investment. Data are free and open to the public through a web query tool and a single CSV download of all data, and the series are republished by the World Bank World Development Indicators and the WHO Global Health Observatory. Caveats: values are annual and national, some are modelled estimates, not reported accounts, and detailed breakdowns exist only for part of the countries. Simulation uses: parameterising the economic side of health system resilience and capacity planning models, comparing investment in facilities across countries, and building scenarios of financial exposure after disasters. Related records: the WHO Global Health Observatory infrastructure indicators (data-who-gho-health-infrastructure-indicators) give beds and facility density to pair with spending.
